title: Identifying the Paid Crossover Lines That Fall on Days a Supplement Policy Did Not Cover
content:
On a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies the paid crossover lines that fall outside cover are identified by comparing the date of service of each paid line with the day the policy took effect. Which lines are counted depends on what the policy record shows about the life of the policy.

1. **Where the policy took effect within the period its paid lines fall in** — the lines counted are those the supplement paid whose date of service falls before the day the policy took effect.
2. **Where the policy stood ended and was afterwards put back in force** — the lines counted are those whose date of service falls in the 12 months to date but outside the period since it was put back in force.
3. **Where neither of those holds** — no line falls outside cover, the policy having been in force for every day its paid lines fall on.

### What each case measures against

The first case measures every paid line against a single date, the day the policy took effect, and counts those rendered before it. It reaches back over the whole of the policy's paid lines, however old.

The second case measures against two boundaries at once: the line must fall within the 12 months to date, and it must fall outside the period since the policy was put back in force. A line rendered more than 12 months ago is not counted in this case however far outside cover it falls, and a line rendered since the policy was put back in force is not counted however recent.

### Hypothetical dates

A policy that took effect on a day falling in the middle of the run of its paid lines: the lines rendered before that day are counted, and those rendered on or after it are not.

A policy that lapsed and was afterwards put back in force: a line rendered 4 months ago, while the policy stood ended, falls within the 12 months to date and outside the period since it was put back in force, so it is counted. A line rendered 15 months ago does not fall within the 12 months to date and is not counted.

A policy in force continuously since before the earliest of its paid lines, never ended: neither case is reached and no line falls outside cover.
